name: Kimberlyn King-Hinds

data_centers.summary: No public statements found on AI data centers as of Sept 2026. Her energy work is about lowering the Northern Mariana Islands' own high electricity bills and replacing imported diesel, with no link to data centers.

evidence.title: Press release: King-Hinds introduces Affordable Power for the Northern Marianas Act (H.R. 10074)
evidence.quote: For too long, our families and businesses have been asked to absorb the cost of an electric system that is too expensive, too old, too fragile, and increasingly difficult to maintain
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants federal Covenant money redirected to cut CNMI electric rates and rebuild the grid; the release never mentions data centers or AI, so it is not a data center position.

evidence.title: Press release: House passes King-Hinds amendments in FY2027 defense bill (Saipan geothermal study)
evidence.quote: Every time there is instability overseas, families in the Northern Mariana Islands feel it in their electric bills
evidence.what_it_shows: Her energy focus is ratepayer costs and moving the islands off imported diesel, not the power demands of AI data centers.

ai_risk.summary: No public position found on AI safety rules, chatbots, deepfakes or AI liability as of Sept 2026. Her one AI-related bill is a narrow cosponsorship letting investigators use face-matching to identify child abuse victims.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Renewed Hope Act (H.R. 6998), lets investigators use facial recognition to identify children in abuse images
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a specific law enforcement use of AI to rescue child victims; it does not speak to whether advanced AI needs safety rules.

tech_regulation.summary: No public position found on Big Tech, Section 230, kids online safety or privacy law as of Sept 2026. The closest item is a 2025 letter backing federal stablecoin standards and strong anti-money-laundering safeguards for Tinian's municipal stablecoin, which is crypto regulation rather than Big Tech regulation.

evidence.title: Letter to Tinian leaders on federal stablecoin regulation and the MUSD stablecoin, reported by Marianas Variety
evidence.quote: I support your efforts to adopt strong internal standards from the outset, particularly those aligned with best practices in anti-money laundering, countering the financing of terrorism and know-your-customer protocols.
evidence.what_it_shows: She is comfortable with federal rules for digital assets and wants safeguards built in early; this is about crypto, not social media or Big Tech, so it does not set a tech regulation score.

preemption.summary: No public position found on federal preemption of state AI laws as of Sept 2026. As a non-voting delegate she had no roll call on the 2025 moratorium, and she did not sign the Matsui or Clarke letters or the March 2026 House leadership statement, and cosponsored none of the preemption bills.

china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. Her China commentary is about keeping visa-free Chinese tourism to the islands, not semiconductors.

signature: No notable public AI activity found; a non-voting delegate focused on CNMI electricity costs, tourism, veterans and territorial fairness, who sits in the Crypto and STEM Education caucuses.
search_notes: Ran about 20 Google News queries (name plus artificial intelligence, AI, data center, electricity/ratepayers, chatbot/deepfake/Take It Down, Big Tech/Section 230/TikTok, Nvidia/export controls/chips, preemption/moratorium/executive order, broadband/undersea cable, crypto/STEM, Renewed Hope Act, Saipan Tribune and Marianas Variety site-scoped searches) and a Wayback listing of king-hinds.house.gov. Read all five pages of her official press release index (Jan 2025 to Sept 2026), the in-the-news and newsletter indexes, the committees and caucuses page, and about 15 individual pages (Affordable Power Act, NDAA amendments, fuel cost letter, OBBB Medicaid statement, NDAA conference, stablecoin letter, Roll Call Feb 2026 interview, Islands Business 2024 debate, Public Radio Guam energy bill story, Guam Daily Post citizenship story). Zero hits for artificial intelligence, AI, data center, deepfake, chatbot, Section 230, export controls or preemption in her own materials or in press coverage. Nothing on the Dec 2025 AI executive order or the March 2026 White House framework. She is a non-voting delegate, so no floor votes exist, including on the July 2025 Senate moratorium vote. No AI caucus or AI task force membership; caucus page lists Crypto and STEM Education among others. No AI super PAC support or attacks found. The Roll Call interview shows her pushing back on Republican senators who want to end the China visa waiver for CNMI tourism, which is unrelated to chips. congress.gov and govtrack member pages were blocked or misrouted, so the single relevant cosponsorship (Renewed Hope Act) comes from the verified record file.
